page: Microsoft Azure DC16ads_cc_v5 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor. This instance features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 614 GB of local storage. The virtualized environment is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2701.38. Multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench scores fall within the average range, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 9808.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 21803.65. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory write operations; while read-only small block memory bandwidth is average at 1036.67 GB/sec, the large block uncached write bandwidth is weak, scoring in the bottom 25% at 22.69 GB/sec. Large block uncached read bandwidth remains average at 39.67 GB/sec.

For workloads, the server demonstrates average performance across database operations, static web serving, and software compilation. It achieves 15.98 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 16.97 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. LLM inference speeds for text generation using a small 135M model are strong at 298.55 tokens/sec, though prompt processing and larger 7B model execution remain average. Given the dedicated AMD EPYC hardware and bundled 614 GB local storage, this server offers balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads, database hosting, and moderate text processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure DC16ads_cc_v5 is an x86_64 general-purpose server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 16 vCPUs, 8 physical cores, and a 3.525 GHz clock speed. It is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM and 614 GB of local storage. Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance and strong text generation speeds for small LLM models. However, a key tradeoff is its weak large-block uncached memory write bandwidth, which falls in the bottom 25%. Most other metrics, including multi-core processing, software compilation, and database operations, perform in the average tier. This server is suited for general-purpose computing, database hosting, and web serving workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources and local storage.
